record.context_brief: Fractal Weyl law for resonance counting
record.original_question: For an open chaotic quantum scattering system with hyperbolic trapped set of Minkowski dimension 1 + 2 nu, what is the sharp asymptotic counting law for long-living resonances? Equivalently, in a fixed high-frequency window [k, k + W] - i[0, gamma] or in the semiclassical strip [E - C hbar, E + C hbar] - i[0, gamma hbar], is the number of resonances of order hbar^(-nu), and does there exist a nontrivial profile F(gamma) such that the count equals C F(gamma) hbar^(-nu) + o(hbar^(-nu))?

evidence.quote:
Questions:
   (1) For given width W > 0 and depth gamma > 0, what is the asymptotic number of
       resonances in the rectangle [k, k + W ] - i[0, gamma] when k -> infinity?

We define the weak, resp. strong form of fractal Weyl law conjecture as follows. (i) Weak form. ... #(Res P(hbar) intersect [E - C hbar, E + C hbar] - i[0, gamma hbar]) >= C C_gamma hbar^(-nu) ... (ii) Strong form. There exists an increasing function F : R+ -> R+ , nonidentically vanishing, such that, for any C, gamma > 0, #(Res P(hbar) intersect [E - C hbar, E + C hbar] - i[0, gamma hbar]) = C F(gamma) hbar^(-nu) + o(hbar^(-nu)), when hbar -> 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P(\hbar)$ be a semiclassical Schrödinger-type operator (e.g. $P(\hbar) = -\hbar^2 \Delta + V$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $V$ smooth and compactly supported, or a more general black-box semiclassical operator) describing an open quantum chaotic scattering system at energy $E > 0$. Assume the classical Hamiltonian flow on the energy shell $\{p = E\}$ admits a trapped set $K_E$ which is a hyperbolic invariant set of Minkowski (box) dimension $1 + 2\nu$, where $0 \le \nu < (n-1)/2$. Let $\mathrm{Res}\,P(\hbar)$ denote the set of quantum resonances of $P(\hbar)$, defined via meromorphic continuation of the resolvent.

Equivalently, in the high-frequency setting, consider an obstacle or potential scattering problem on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with a hyperbolic trapped set of Minkowski dimension $1 + 2\nu$, and let resonances $k_j$ live in the lower half-plane $\{\mathrm{Im}\, k \le 0\}$.

Prove or disprove the following two forms of the fractal Weyl law:

(i) Weak form. For every $C > 0$ and every $\gamma > 0$ there exists $c_\gamma > 0$ such that, as $\hbar \to 0$,
$$\#\bigl(\mathrm{Res}\,P(\hbar) \cap ([E - C\hbar, E + C\hbar] - i[0, \gamma\hbar])\bigr) \;\ge\; c_\gamma \, \hbar^{-\nu}.$$

(ii) Strong form. There exists a non-decreasing, not identically zero function $F : (0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ such that, for every $C > 0$ and every $\gamma > 0$,
$$\#\bigl(\mathrm{Res}\,P(\hbar) \cap ([E - C\hbar, E + C\hbar] - i[0, \gamma\hbar])\bigr) \;=\; C\, F(\gamma)\, \hbar^{-\nu} + o(\hbar^{-\nu}), \qquad \hbar \to 0.$$

Equivalently, in the high-frequency formulation, given a window $W > 0$ and depth $\gamma > 0$, determine the asymptotics as $k \to \infty$ of the number of resonances in the rectangle $[k, k + W] - i[0, \gamma]$, and decide whether it is of order $k^{\nu}$ with a nontrivial profile in $\gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: Sharp upper bounds of the conjectured order $\hbar^{-\nu}$ are known in considerable generality (Sjöstrand–Zworski, Nonnenmacher–Zworski and others), and matching lower bounds (and even an exact asymptotic) have been proved for open quantum chaotic maps by Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski (Annals of Math., 2014). For genuine Schrödinger / obstacle scattering operators, the lower-bound (weak form) and the existence of a universal profile $F(\gamma)$ (strong form) remain open in general; numerical and experimental evidence (e.g. three-disk scattering) supports the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Nonnenmacher, Sjöstrand, Zworski establish a fractal Weyl law (matching upper and lower bounds) for open quantum chaotic maps, a model setting for the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proven for the toy model of open quantum chaotic maps.

status_evidence.title: Resonance states of the three-disk scattering system
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical validation of the fractal Weyl law over a wide range of wavenumbers in three-disk scattering.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence supports the fractal Weyl law in physical chaotic scattering systems, but a rigorous proof for Schrödinger/obstacle scattering is not established.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl Laws for Chaotic Open Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Lu, Sridhar, Zworski formulated and tested the fractal Weyl law conjecture for chaotic open systems.
status_evidence.claim: Original physics-level statement of the conjecture, motivating the mathematical formulation.
